classification.difficultyReason: Use the supplied definition of break-even to locate the cost–revenue intersection, then read its horizontal coordinate as cards and vertical coordinate as revenue.

content.prompt: Suzy makes hand-painted cards. The production cost and the revenue generated by the sale of the cards can be modelled with two linear equations and shown on a graph.

spec.description: Cost and revenue graph with unit-spaced horizontal-axis grid and 7.5-dollar vertical-axis grid. Red revenue and blue cost retain the source's series distinction; no intersection marker or equations are supplied.
spec.mathematics: Revenue joins (0,0) to (40,240); cost joins (0,60) to (40,140). Their intersection is (15,90).
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied series, labels and grid are visible; no answer annotation.

children.label: a
children.prompt: In business, “breaking even” means that revenue from selling items is equal to the cost of producing the items. How many cards does Suzy need to sell to break even?

answer.worked: The cost and revenue lines intersect at 15 cards. Suzy needs to sell 15 cards to break even.

children.label: b
children.prompt: What is the revenue at this break-even point?

answer.worked: The vertical coordinate of the intersection is 90, so the revenue at break-even is $\$90$.
